page: Amazon Web Services m7i.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 16 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supported by a 105 MB L3 cache. System memory consists of 64.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and 8-bit integer operations. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates average performance across most workloads. The stress-ng single-core CPU score is 1909.39, while the multi-core score reaches 14645.49. Cryptographic capabilities are supported by hardware-accelerated AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instructions, yielding a PassMark CPU encryption test score of 15072.68.

The DDR5 memory subsystem delivers a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 1181.52 GB/sec and an uncached large block read bandwidth of 75.78 GB/sec. Network connectivity is configured with a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps. For specialized workloads, the instance achieves a top-tier result in LLM text generation for small (135M) models, processing 333.79 tokens per second. However, medium (7B) model text generation drops to an average tier of 15.01 tokens per second, and large (70B) model inference is unsupported due to memory and hardware constraints.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m7i.4xlarge offers a balanced resource profile suitable for general-purpose enterprise applications. The absence of bundled local storage requires reliance on external network-attached storage, which represents a structural tradeoff for I/O-heavy workloads. This instance is configured for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, database operations, and moderate-scale machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs and 8 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, but lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Benchmark results place the instance in the average tier for general compute, memory bandwidth, and database operations, though it achieves top-tier performance in text generation for small LLM models. With a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps, the m7i.4xlarge is suited for balanced workloads including software compilation, web serving, database operations, and general-purpose enterprise applications that do not require high-speed local NVMe storage.
